newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE EXPORTS 100,000 TONNES OF MAIZE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE EXPORTS 100,000 TONNES OF MAIZE.

text.p: Zimbabwe has exported around 100,000 tonnes of maize since the beginning of the April-March marketing season, a senior official of the state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB) said on Tuesday.
The official told reporters the maize was sold mainly to Japan, Venezuela and Angola and was part of the 250,000 tonnes the GMB set aside earlier this year as an export quota, its first since 1991.

The southern African state estimates its maize production quadruppled to 2.6 million in the growing season that ended in March after production was hit by a severe drought in 1994 and the previous two years.
The GMB official said the remainder of the 1996/97 export quota was still available.
The official said Zimbabwe was currently considering enquiries from Germany about its remaining export stocks, but declined to give further details.
